items.title: 14.9.1 Major air pollutants and their health effects

blocks.text: Particulate matter consists of tiny particles suspended in the air, including dust, dirt, soot and smoke, from 2.5 micrometres to 10 micrometres in diameter; inhaling it causes inflammation and irritation of the airways, leading to conditions such as asthma and bronchitis. Short-term exposure to nitrogen dioxide and sulfur dioxide irritates the respiratory system, while long-term exposure raises the risk of respiratory infection, asthma and bronchitis.
